cards.details: Oral transmission of the teachings of Mahavira, known as the Purvas.
First Jain Council held to codify the 12 Angas; loss of the 14 Purvas.
Devarddhi Gani Kshamashramana oversaw the final compilation and redaction of the Shvetambara canon.

items.title: A-U-P-P
items.decryption: The hierarchy of Shvetambara canonical literature: The 12 Angas are the primary texts, followed by 12 Upangas (subsidiary).

items: Do not confuse 'Purvas' (early texts) with 'Agamas' (canonical texts); Purvas are largely considered lost.
Digambara sect does not accept the Shvetambara canon as authentic; they rely on their own tradition of Sharavanabelagola/Mathura texts.
Jain literature was primarily written in Prakrit (Ardha-Magadhi, Shauraseni) and later in Sanskrit, not Pali (which is Buddhist).

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Linguistics

  • Ardha-Magadhi: Original language
  • Shauraseni: Used in Digambara texts
  • Sanskrit: Used in later period philosophy

Key Thinkers

  • Bhadrabahu: Expert in Purvas
  • Sthulabhadra: Led Pataliputra Council
  • Devarddhi Gani: Valabhi compilation

Structure of Jain Literature

  • Agama Literature (Shvetambara)
    • 12 Angas (The primary limbs)
    • 12 Upangas (Secondary texts)
    • 10 Prakirnas (Miscellaneous topics)
    • 6 Chedasutras (Monastic conduct)
  • Non-Canonical Texts
    • Works of Haribhadra Suri
    • Hemachandra's 'Trishashthishalakapurushacharitra'
    • Jinasena’s 'Adipurana'
